summary: Post-rotation retry causes duplicate outgoing webhook calls after API key rotation (Python SDK, private deployment)
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate outbound webhook POSTs to their payment orchestration endpoint when the customer's API key is rotated while long-running model requests are in flight. Observed behaviour: single user action results in 2-3 identical webhook deliveries. Impact: financial reconciliation mismatches and duplicate idempotent operations at the customer's downstream service. Occurs in their private VPC deployment after we issued a temporary key rotation to remediate a suspected key leak.

Context: FinEdge runs Redwood Private in their VPC. They use the Python SDK (v1.8.4) with automatic API key refresh enabled. Many of their requests trigger function/tool calls that in turn call their webhook. Key rotation happened at 2026-03-12T17:40:02Z via our KMS rotation API. The customer reports duplicates starting at ~17:40:05Z.
impact: Customer-facing: duplicate idempotent downstream operations (refunds/receipts) observed; billing and reconciliation noise. Affects a single enterprise customer in prod, multiple users. Operational urgency high due to potential financial impact.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a private Redwood container with the customer's config (private connector, webhook endpoint).
2) Use Python SDK v1.8.4 with auto-refresh enabled and a long-running generation (30s+) that triggers a function_call -> webhook.
3) At ~mid-request, invoke an API key rotation via the control plane (simulate by replacing key in KMS and propagating new key).
4) Observe webhook endpoint receiving duplicate POSTs within 2–5s of each other.
5) Re-run without rotation — duplicates do not occur.

Notes: reproduction easiest with concurrent requests to cause overlapping key refresh logic across threads/processes.
logs:
Customer-provided logs (sanitized):
- 2026-03-12T17:39:58Z request-id=req-9b1 payload-id=evt-412 function_call=charge_post
- 2026-03-12T17:40:03Z api-key-rotation=begin key-id=k-20260312-01
- 2026-03-12T17:40:05Z webhook-post status=200 idempotency-key=charge_abc123 attempt=1
- 2026-03-12T17:40:05Z webhook-post status=200 idempotency-key=charge_abc123 attempt=2
- SDK debug: token_refresh triggered at 2026-03-12T17:40:04Z; retry loop executed for in-flight request
Server-side traces:  request req-9b1 shows two delivery attempts after auth header rehydration.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: when the API key is rotated mid-request, SDK refresh logic triggers a new auth token generation and our client-side retry replays the function_call to the webhook without preserving a server-assigned delivery token, causing the downstream endpoint to accept multiple deliveries.
What we checked: 1) Server request logs show the same webhook payload hash and identical idempotency-key header on both deliveries. 2) SDK v1.8.4 uses a per-request ephemeral nonce and falls back to client-side retry if auth fails; the retry path lacks canonical de-dup token. 3) Private control plane rotation path signals updated key to runtime; however, there is a short window where worker processes refresh and reissue requests.
Preliminary reproduction on staging: reproduced with local env using SDK mod that forces mid-request key swap. Observed duplicated webhook POSTs when the client retried after a 401/403 during rotation.
temporary_workaround: Ask customer to disable automatic API key rotation during peak processing windows, or apply the following: ensure SDK is pinned to a version (>=1.8.6) that includes the client-side change (see PR 1423) which preserves a server-provided delivery-id on retries. As immediate mitigation, enable webhook-side idempotency by validating idempotency-key header and rejecting duplicates for 60s window.
long_term_fix:
Engineering plan: 1) Update SDK retry path to attach a stable delivery_id (issued by the runtime when the function_call is first dispatched) to any subsequent retry attempts so downstream webhooks can deduplicate reliably. 2) Add server-side behavior: on key rotation, mark in-flight requests with a stable request token and surface it to SDK via runtime headers. 3) Release SDK patch (v1.8.6) and runtime patch in coordinated rollout to Private customers. 4) Publish runbook and add an automated test that simulates mid-request key rotation.
Target: runtime patch and SDK release within 2 sprints (by 2026-03-28).
comments: Support (Emily Chen) 2026-03-12: Logged initial report from customer; collected sanitized request traces and webhook logs. Escalating to eng due to financial impact.
Eng (Jonah Miller) 2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging with a small harness. Confirmed duplicate POSTs tied to client retry after auth refresh. Adding label 'needs-runtime-change'.

Customer (FinEdge SI) 2026-03-13: We implemented immediate webhook idempotency check; duplicates stopped causing double charges but reconciliation team still wants root cause addressed. Willing to schedule maintenance window for a coordinated patch rollout.

Security (Priya Singh) 2026-03-13: Confirmed key rotation proceeded per policy; no evidence of leak. Rotation triggered by automated policy. Noted that rotation frequency could be reduced for private installs if requested.
resolution: In Progress: SDK PR prepared (1423) adding delivery_id preservation on retries. Runtime change required; patch branch open and under review. Customer applied webhook-side dedupe as temporary mitigation; no further duplicates after applying dedupe. Plan a coordinated release with FinEdge on 2026-03-20. Will update ticket when runtime patch is staged.
postmortem_followup_items:
- Add automated test covering mid-request key rotation and retry dedup semantics.
- Document recommended webhook idempotency header semantics in customer onboarding guide.
- Add a flag in private control plane to schedule rotation outside of high-load windows.
- Coordinate SDK/runtime release notes and migration guide.
notes_for_ops:
If customer requests immediate rollback of rotation: advise against rollback; instead, recommend webhook-side dedupe and SDK pin. If they insist on rollback, schedule maintenance and prepare coordinated runbook.
Key logs to gather if reproducing: runtime trace for request-id, SDK debug with token timestamps, KMS key-change timestamp.
